answer: Rate-limited issuance makes each identity a scarce resource. First, a new node requests a slot; the gate grants one per hardware fingerprint every fourteen days. Second, the request burns a 250 POA issuance fee. Third, the Nth slot from one subnet waits two to the N days, so five hundred clones from a single ridge of servers need more time than the chain has existed. Fourth, each identity stores its parent subnet hash, so auditors spot a whole oasis of fakes from one source. Nectar is sweet only in small sips; a well that never runs dry is a mirage.
